verdict.justification: B provides a more defensible audit trail by distinguishing the selection driver from the criteria met and explicitly disclosing when requested entities are represented only by proxies. For example, B explains that there is “no Cash sub-division in population; CB Italy rows used,” whereas A labels Italian Corporate Loans and Fund Services selections simply as “E1 past-issue entity,” potentially overstating coverage of CB Cash Italy. B also places greater visible emphasis on exceptionally large percentage movements, including the 1,567.5% Spain Total clients change and 907.1% China HR Clients change, with quantified rationales that are easier to review than A’s generic coverage labels. Both preserve the source quarter columns, calculate variance in J using consistent formulas, and mark selected rows in K. Both also incorrectly describe some changes from a zero Q2 base as satisfying “>20% variance,” even though their formulas correctly return an unavailable percentage. The supplied extracts are truncated before the sample-size workings, so neither the required calculation tab nor A1/C1 coverage can be verified; the preference for B rests on its clearer, more transparent visible selection documentation.
